items.title: Morning Briefing Oct. 19, 2026
items.excerpt: Here's a rundown of all the news you need to start your Monday, including US President Donald Trump holding off on new measures against Russia, four people dying and dozens seriously wounded in fire at Canadian military base, US Embassy in UAE urging Americans in Middle East to exercise ‘heightened vigilance,' and fresh clashes erupting in Paris as France protest arrests exceed 2,000. US President Donald Trump said Sunday that he would not sign a document imposing additional measures on Russia for now, arguing that doing so could undermine negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. “My decision on Russia is a very simple one,” he said in a post on his Truth Social platform, adding that he was negotiating peace between Russia and Ukraine and did not want to take an action that would “drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table.” Trump said “great progress” was being made in the negotiations, including ongoing “hostage negotiations.” He said he could sign the document at a later date or “any time” he wanted. The president did not provide details about the negotiations or identify the hostages to whom he was referring. - Carney says 4 killed, dozens seriously wounded in fire at Canadian military base Four people were killed and dozens more seriously wounded after a fast-moving fire swept through a Canadian military base in Alberta, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Sunday, describing the incident as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for the country's armed forces. “I regret that I can confirm at this time that Forest Service members have lost their lives, and their next of kin has been notified. Dozens more are seriously wounded,” Carney told reporters. The blaze broke out on Saturday afternoon at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, about 200 kilometers (124 miles) southeast of Edmonton, spreading beyond a training area as strong winds hampered firefighting efforts. “Yesterday afternoon, a violent, fast-moving fire swept through Canadian Armed Forces base in Wainwright, Alberta,” he said. “What followed was one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime.” - US Embassy in UAE urges Americans in Middle East to exercise ‘heightened vigilance’ The US Embassy in the United Arab Emirates issued a security alert warning Americans in the Middle East to exercise heightened vigilance amid a complex security environment, citing potential flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruptions. It said Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi group had carried out attacks against Saudi Arabia including strikes on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure that caused civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. “The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area,” the statement said. The embassy urged Americans traveling to or from the Middle East to monitor airport and airline operations and prepare contingency plans in advance. - Fresh clashes erupt in Paris as France protest arrests exceed 2,000 French police used tear gas and a water cannon against protesters in central Paris on Sunday, a day after nationwide cost-of-living demonstrations were marred by violence that resulted in more than 2,000 arrests. Fresh tensions erupted at Place de la Republique following social media calls for a gathering, Le Parisien reported. Police made several arrests, while some protesters erected barricades and firefighters tackled a blaze on nearby Rue Yves-Toudic. Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron emphasized the need to maintain law and order and restore calm, announcing that prefects could prohibit certain demonstrations. ... Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced an updated nationwide tally of more than 2,000 arrests following Saturday’s unrest, during which over 600 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured. items.title: Treasury yields move lower as investors assess U.S. inflation backdrop
items.excerpt: Treasury yields moved higher on Monday as investors continue to weigh the domestic inflation and interest rate backdrop against broader geopolitical developments. The yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury Add To Watchlist — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — rose more than 1 basis point to 5.11%. The longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasury Add To Watchlist bond yield — which often moves on geopolitical developments — was also more than 1 basis point higher at 5.448%. The yield on the 2-year Treasury note Add To Watchlist, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, was up more than 2 basis points at 4.757%. One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another. The moves lower come despite inflation concerns continuing to loom over the U.S. economy. Last week's strong inflation data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics saw wholesale prices rise 6.3% annually last month — the biggest jump since 2022 — with consumer costs up 3.7% annually in September, beating estimates. Meanwhile, energy prices fell Monday as investors continued to weigh the possibility of more Russian crude supply coming onto the market. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures Add To Watchlist for November delivery were down 0.6% at $100.73 per barrel. Brent crude Add To Watchlist, the global oil price benchmark, dropped 1.6% to $108.13. With the Federal Reserve's next interest rate decision due Oct. 28, traders are now pricing in an above-85% probability that the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee will leave borrowing costs unchanged, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

items.title: Hassett says inflation "needing some work" By Investing.com
items.excerpt: Investing.com -- White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said Monday that inflation requires policy attention after September consumer price data showed continued pressure, though prices have declined for some items including beef and eggs. "If you look at the previous three months, it looked like inflation was completely under control, and now it looks like it's sort of back needing some work," Hassett told CNBC Monday. Consumer price data released last week showed prices rose in September at the fastest pace in five months. The consumer price index increased 0.6% from the previous month. A measure of underlying price pressures that excludes food and energy rose 0.3%, exceeding expectations. "This is either a sort of break from the downtrend or a blip," Hassett said in the interview. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh last week did not address market expectations that the central bank will keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting later this month. During a moderated discussion at the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings, Warsh made no comments on monetary policy or his economic outlook beyond stating the Fed will deliver price stability. Hassett said he respects the central bank's independence and noted Warsh will "do what he thinks is the right thing." ... "People are really euphoric about how well the economy is doing, and they're spending more. And of course, that's the kind of thing the Fed needs to pay attention to," Hassett said.

items.title: United States: October inflation seen cooling – TD Securities
items.excerpt: TD Securities economists Oscar Munoz and Eli Nir project that US headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) will rise 0.30% month-on-month in October 2026, slowing from September’s 0.65% gain, with gasoline and food still contributing. They expect core CPI to increase 0.21% and translate into a 0.24% rise in core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, as core goods and services inflation moderate and shelter cools. ## TD sees softer but still solid CPI ... "Following the release of the September CPI report, we are providing an early look into our October projection based on multiple assumptions which may evolve as the month progresses and more data becomes available — particularly for volatile segments like gasoline prices, hotel rates, and airfares." ... "Headline inflation is expected to cool down in October, rising a still solid 0.30% m/m after a stronger 0.65% m/m September increase (CPI NSA index: 337.316 vs the market's current fixing at 337.250)." "Our preliminary forecast for the October core CPI stands at 0.21% m/m (down from a firmer 0.33% gain in September), which would be consistent with a core PCE increase at 0.24%." "Core goods prices likely lost some momentum on the back of a decline in used vehicle prices and cooling from apparel, recreation and IT goods. A pickup in household goods prices likely acted as a partial offset to the broad decline." ... "Services inflation is projected to mean-revert following last month's broad-based increase. We look for shelter to throttle down — led by a reversal in OER — after an unexpected surge in the last report. Slowing inflation in transportation and recreation services is also expected to help tame price gains in the segment."

items.title: Emma Freud says Beatles' songs to star in Yesterday musical
items.excerpt: Emma Freud says Beatles' songs to star in Yesterday musical # Freud confirms Beatles' songs to star in musical 18 minutes ago Mariam Issimdar Jeff Spicer/Getty Images Screenwriter Richard Curtis and his wife Emma Freud are looking to bring the movie Yesterday on to the theatre stage Film producer Emma Freud has confirmed The Beatles have agreed for their songs to feature in a stage version of the movie, Yesterday. Freud is working on the show with her husband, Richard Curtis. They were behind the 2019 film and other box office hits, including Love Actually and Bridget Jones's Diary. She called it "a huge deal", saying: "They've [The Beatles] never done that with a West End musical before. So it's the first time that you can kind of legally see The Beatles' music on stage, which is amazing." Freud spoke to BBC Radio Suffolk on Monday, after she received an honorary doctorate for her work in film and broadcasting at the University of Suffolk on Saturday. University of Suffolk Emma Freud received an honorary doctorate in Ipswich on Saturday She said a theatre where the stage show will be performed had been chosen - "but I can't tell you what it is because I will get killed". She confirmed the stage version of Yesterday would also be directed by Oscar-winner Danny Boyle, who oversaw the movie. Freud said: "We're at workshop stages, so we've already had two workshops and we've got a third one coming up this month, where you sort of ask actors to come into a room and just interrogate the script and the songs and the staging, and see how it's going to work. "Currently we're on the 11th draft of the script, because it isn't just taking a movie script and putting it on to a stage. "It's the same story, but actually every beat of it becomes different, becomes theatrical rather than filmic. "So it's been an incredible process to be a part of. I don't feel like I've ever done anything as big in my entire life." The Beatles were one of the biggest bands on the planet, with a multitude of hits including Hey Jude, Let it Be and Yesterday Yesterday is about a struggling musician who wakes up one day to find an altered world where no-one has heard of The Beatles. He becomes famous after singing their songs and passing them off as his own. The film stars Himesh Patel and Lily James, along with Suffolk-based singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran. It was shot throughout Suffolk, Essex and Norfolk, including a scene with 6,000 extras in Gorleston-on-Sea. Richard Curtis with the lead actor in the film Yesterday, Himesh Patel On receiving her doctorate from the University of Suffolk, Freud said "the honour" was "so massive", because "Suffolk is my home and it's where I was brought up, and it's where my family has lived for generations". Her family arrived in the county as Jewish refugees from Germany in the 1930s, escaping the tyranny of the Nazis

The sequel has witnessed a significant surge in its worldwide earnings, reportedly nearing the ₹425 crore mark within just four days of release. ... ## Jailer 2 Opening Weekend Worldwide Box Office Collection: Rajinikanth's Film Nears XXX Cr Mark Globally Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 continued its strong box office run on Sunday, October 18, recording an increase in domestic net collections on its fourth day in theatres. The Tamil action comedy, which arrived in cinemas worldwide on October 15, has accumulated ₹199.90 crore in India net collections, according to Sacnilk. Its worldwide gross collection has reached ₹424.25 crore after four days. The film collected an estimated ₹55.85 crore net across India on Day 4, registering an 18.2% increase over Saturday's reported collection of ₹47.25 crore. Sunday's performance also took the film's total India gross to ₹234.25 crore. Overseas markets contributed another ₹40 crore on the fourth day, bringing the cumulative overseas gross to ₹190 crore.

items.excerpt: What to Stream: 'Moana,' 'Modern Warfare 4,' Dolly Parton tribute, 'Lupin' and John Legend ... John Legend's new album titled “Muse,” produced by Pharrell Williams, is among the new streaming releases coming the week of Oct. 19. The live-action “Moana,” featuring Dwayne Johnson as Maui,” debuts Wednesday on Disney+. The original animated version is also available. On Friday, “The Invite,” starring Seth Rogen and Olivia Wilde, streams on HBO Max. In gaming, “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4" launches Friday, this time set on the Korean Peninsula. “Nintendo Switch Sports Resort” arrives Thursday, offering 12 events including bowling and tennis for up to eight players online. New television series include the fourth season of Netflix's “Lupin” and a three-episode “Vanderpump Rules” series set in Las Vegas. Paramount's “Street Fighter” leads the box office this weekend, earning $31 million from 3,575 theaters in the U.S. and Canada. However, the spotlight is on the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything,” which made an impressive $15 million from just 855 screens. Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the film has received rave reviews and a 99% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Meanwhile, the survival thriller “Whalefall” underperformed, earning $8 million domestically. The weekend's overall ticket sales reached about $101.6 million, marking a 45% increase from last year. ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (AP) — A New Mexico judge has dismissed a grand jury indictment that accused actor Timothy Busfield him of four counts of criminal sexual contact with a child. The judge cited prosecutorial misconduct and errors that undermined the grand jury process. The case stems from when Busfield was directing the TV series “The Cleaning Lady.” Busfield denied the allegations, describing them as a vendetta pursued by the parents of two boys who were let go from the show. His attorneys said prosecutors suppressed evidence and restricted grand jury testimony. Prosecutors disputed those claims. NEW YORK (AP) — Selma Blair's representatives have stated she did not intend to harm anyone during a recent flight incident. Blair, who has multiple sclerosis, experienced a medical emergency on a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York. She was accused of injuring two flight attendants and later kicking a police officer and a nurse. Her representatives emphasized that Blair's condition can cause episodes that may be misunderstood. Blair pleaded not guilty to assault charges and is free on bail. The FBI has also charged her with assault related to her actions on the plane. Blair has been a vocal advocate for disability rights. ... NEW YORK (AP) — Superhero films and horror have usually stayed on separate sides of the multiplex. But DC Studios' “Clayface” is the rare attempt to meld the two movie genres. “Clayface” is something unusual in the normally calculated realm of comic book movies. It’s R-rated. It’s also modestly budgeted at $40 million. And it stars the relatively unknown Tom Rhys Harries as a little-known DC villain. And it comes at a pivotal time for James Gunn and Peter Safran's DC Studios, following the box-office flop of “Supergirl” and the Warner Bros. merger with Paramount. ... “La Bola Negra” is a Spanish flim that explores the lives of gay men in Spain in 1932, 1937 and 2017. Directed by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, the film draws inspiration from Federico García Lorca and Alberto Conejero’s works. It weaves stories of love, war and generational trauma, featuring a standout debut by Guitarricadelafuente. In her review for The Associated Press, film writer Lindsey Bahr writes that the film, despite some stylistic weight, is a remarkably transfixing exercise and exploration of the caustic ripple effects of repression and silence. Rated R, the film is in theaters now and will be on Netflix in December.
